# Additional site references — 2026-10-08

Four unmodified original photographs by 朱華龍 - Zhu Hua Long (CC BY 2.0) are collected with full attribution, license, original source URL and matching published Commons SHA-1 plus local SHA-256. Directly reviewed originals fill Qiushuang architecture slot 2, Hengwu architecture slot 2 and lattice/material slot 3, and Daoxiang architecture slot 2. Total collection is 12/42, leaving 30 slots. The strict all-reference audit still rejects incomplete coverage.

The named entrance plaques identify the three architectural sites. The close ice-crack screen supports Hengwu's specified wall kit; the photographed interior itself is not asserted to be Hengwu. Daoxiang's modern photographed roof is tiled, so it does not replace the project's actual thatch, low rough fence or painted paddy. Its separate close material and night-set requirements remain open. None of these daylight photographs fills a Shaw Brothers night-set slot or becomes a shipped texture.

The public Commons category [Beijing Daguanyuan](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Beijing_Daguanyuan) has 145 file records. Two imageinfo continuation responses supplied the records omitted by its initial 50-item thumbnail limit. All 145 thumbnails were reviewed in five contact sheets; selected originals were downloaded and checked separately. An initial parser failed on omitted imageinfo before saving; the corrected collector saves raw responses and completes the continuation. An original download batch hit HTTP 429 after two successes. The later sequential collector preserves those files, verifies three more originals and stops on a 600-second Retry-After for the next request. No refused original is counted. Raw candidates remain in the temporary review folder rather than the final collection.

Each final site folder retains the complete imageinfo metadata for its accepted files. `sources.json` and the site sheet explain exact relevance and limitations. The collection was independent of the running painted-moon lighting refresh; no scene geometry, lights, runtime or package changed in this reference pass.

## Follow-up collection

The later sequential request succeeds for two more originals, with published SHA-1 and local SHA-256 verified. The Xiaoxiang entrance plaque identifies the site; its door, transom and painted beams fill architecture slot 2. Required coverage is now 13/42, leaving 29 slots. The photograph is daylight and does not fill the night-set slot.

The second photograph shows a pierced rock surround around a circular portal. It is retained under `supporting/rockery-gate/` with attribution and original metadata, outside the required-reference catalog. It supplies visible rock cavities, silhouette and path construction, but has no deep tunnel, fog or dark-side view. None of the rockery sheet's three required slots is marked collected by this supporting photograph. Both originals are by 朱華龍 - Zhu Hua Long, CC BY 2.0.
